_comment: TEMPLATE — copy to stack.local.json (gitignored) and list the tools, platforms and vendors YOUR team actually runs. This is what turns industry news into news about you: when a gathered item names something in this file, the brief says so explicitly instead of hedging ('if you use X'). Keep vendor/contract detail out of the public repo — this template ships with placeholders only.
_how_to_use: If config/stack.local.json exists, check every gathered item against it. On a match, lead with the fact that it is ours (see SKILL.md, 'Know your own stack'). Unmatched items stay industry context. Delete the file to disable the check.
_filling_it_in: Best filled with whoever owns the stack (analytics lead, data platform lead). Only list what you genuinely run — a wrong entry produces a confidently wrong 'this is yours'. Add `version` where a version actually matters (a bug notice is only relevant to the versions you run). Use `status` to distinguish what is in production from what is a pilot or under evaluation.

stack.name: <vendor or tool, as it appears in the press, e.g. 'Google Meridian'>
stack.category: <mmm | attribution | incrementality | clean-room | identity | bi | warehouse | transformation | dsp | measurement-vendor | consent | other>
stack.owner: <optional team or role that owns it>
stack.note: <optional: what we use it for, so the brief can say why an item matters>

watch_competitors: <agency or vendor that competes with our offering, e.g. a rival healthcare-marketing agency>
_watch_competitors_note: Names listed here are matched against gathered items so a competitor's product launch can be cross-referenced against the account book (see SKILL.md, 'Cross-brief link'). Competitors are usually public companies, but treat this list as local config anyway.
